title: Exponential Moving Average of Weights in Deep Learning: Dynamics and Benefits
mechanism: EMA of weights as a plug-in gives solutions that generalise better, are more robust to noisy labels, more consistent and better calibrated, with less need for lr decay.
adaptation: Add EMA (decay 0.999 and 0.9998, BN recomputed) to house and PF runs; evaluate EMA vs last iterate from the same runs; targets positional noise in crack labels.
min_experiment: Arm: EMA weights of 5 runs. Baseline: last iterate of the same 5 runs (paired). Metric: crack IoU, relF1@2, inactive IoU on clean 49 / CV; E1 relF1@2. Kill: paired diff < 0.005 crack IoU and < 0.01 E1 relF1@2.
evidence: R: systematic study on image classification; EMA improves generalisation, noisy-label robustness, prediction consistency, calibration and transfer.
prior_overlap: partial: EMA teacher in Mean Teacher runs was within +-0.005 of the student, under SSL losses; supervised EMA on house/PF never varied (BRIEF optimizer row)

alt_notes.adaptation: Add EMA (decay 0.999 and 0.9998) to house and PF; recompute or EMA BN stats. Crack labels are 1-2 px jittered, i.e. label noise, which is where the paper reports EMA helps. Paired raw vs EMA from the same run reduces seed noise (problem 5).
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm PF+EMA vs PF raw weights of the same runs, seeds 5-9. Metric: test clean crack IoU and relF1@2, inactive IoU, E1 crack relF1@2. Kill if EMA - raw < +0.005 relF1@2 paired over 5 seeds and inactive not better.

alt_notes.adaptation: EMA decay 0.999 and 0.9998 on house and PF runs; EMA BN buffers or recompute them; raw vs EMA is paired within a run, which removes seed variance. Crack label jitter is the label noise case.
alt_notes.min_experiment: Arm: PF + EMA (0.999, 0.9998), 5 seeds. Baseline: same runs' raw weights and SUP100-PF. Metric: val relF1@2, then test clean crack relF1@2, crack IoU, E1 relF1@2. Kill: EMA minus raw < +0.005 val relF1@2 paired over 5 seeds.
